evidence: Nestled in the heart of Hà Nội, the Quang Trung Statue stands as a monumental tribute to one of Vietnam's most revered heroes, Emperor Quang Trung, also known as Nguyễn Huệ. This colossal bronze sculpture, erected in 1989, marks the bicentennial celebration of the decisive victory at Ngọc Hồi and Đống Đa, which saw the peasant general lead a swift and strategic campaign against the formidable Qing army, defeating them with a force of just 29,000 Vietnamese soldiers against 290,000 Qing troops in the spring of 1789, the year of the Kỷ Dậu cycle.
